# Code comments

Applies to comments and docstrings only. Never change code behaviour.

Tags: strength (`hard` always · `default` unless an exception or the sensitivity says otherwise · `soft` preference) · kind (`ai-tell`, `clarity`, `both`, `procedure`).

### CMT-001 · comments carry why, not what
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Write a comment only for what the code cannot say: the why behind a constraint, workaround, decision, external quirk or gotcha.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Doc blocks on public declarations (CMT-014); Live TODO/FIXME (CMT-013); Machine-read directives (CMT-011); Files whose established convention is denser commenting (CMT-015)
- Example: ✗ # loop over users and check each one → ✓ # The billing API rejects batches over 100, so send in chunks.

### CMT-002 · deletion test
`default · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Test each comment by deleting it in your head: if a competent reader would recover the same information from the code within seconds, the comment goes.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Comments that record external facts the code cannot show (API limits, legal or protocol requirements)

### CMT-003 · restating / name-narrating / type-echo comment
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not write comments that restate the next line, paraphrase the identifier, or echo types already in the signature.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Languages or projects whose doc tooling requires @param/@returns tags (keep, but say something the type does not); Teaching material and examples written for beginners
- Example: ✗ // get the user by id / function getUserById(id: string): User → ✓ function getUserById(id: string): User

### CMT-004 · terse inline why
`soft · clarity · scope: comments · voice can override`

Keep an inline comment to one short line of non-obvious why; move longer explanation to a doc block, the commit message or the docs.

- Threshold: **standard:** one or two lines · **strict:** one line · **relaxed:** follow the file's existing comment length
- Exceptions: Algorithm or protocol notes that must stay next to the code

### CMT-005 · banner / divider comments
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not add banner or divider comments to mark sections; let functions, files and modules carry the structure.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `// ====`, `// ----`, `# ====`, `# ----`, `#region`, `// #region`, `/* ===`
- Exceptions: The file or project already uses region markers or dividers consistently (criterion 6); Editor-folding markers the project relies on
- Example: ✗ // ===== Helpers ===== → ✓ (no comment; move helpers to their own module if the file needs sections)

### CMT-006 · commented-out code
`default · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not leave commented-out code in a change; version control keeps the old version.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Code samples inside doc blocks or docs; Pre-existing commented-out code outside the change's scope (report, do not delete)

### CMT-007 · diff-anchored / changelog comments
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Describe in comments what the code does and why it is that way now, not the edit that produced it; changelog, attribution and old-ticket notes belong in the commit history.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `added`, `replaced`, `no longer`, `previously`, `now uses`, `updated to`, `changed to`, `refactored`, `fix for bug`, `added by`, `new:`
- Exceptions: A ticket or issue link that encodes a live, actionable constraint (e.g. waiting on an upstream fix); Licence and copyright headers
- Example: ✗ # Updated to use the new cache instead of the old loop → ✓ # Cache lookups; the upstream service is rate-limited.

### CMT-008 · comment apologising for own-code surprise
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not paper over a surprise in code you control with a warning comment; when writing the code, make it unsurprising, and in a prose-only pass keep the true comment and report the surprise as code work.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: The surprise comes from something outside our control (third-party API, platform bug, external contract); A prose-only review pass: never change code to make a comment unnecessary (criterion 1)
- Example: ✗ // careful: this mutates the input, don't call twice → ✓ (when writing new code: return a new value instead; in a comment-only pass: keep the comment and report the mutation as open work)

### CMT-009 · constraint comment -> enforceable encoding
`soft · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

When a comment states a constraint (do not remove, do not reorder, talk to X first), suggest enforcing it with a type, check, test or lint rule, but add the encoding only with the user's approval and delete the comment only once the encoding exists.

- Exceptions: Prose-only passes: report the suggestion; do not add code or tests

### CMT-010 · emphasis-only comments
`default · both · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not write comments whose only content is emphasis (IMPORTANT, NOTE, do not remove); state the concrete reason, and when reviewing such a comment, check the claim against the code before keeping or removing it.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `important:`, `note:`, `critical:`, `warning:`, `do not remove`, `don't touch`, `be careful`
- Exceptions: Conventional markers the project tooling reads (CMT-011)
- Example: ✗ // IMPORTANT: do not remove! → ✓ // Payment webhooks retry on 5xx; this must stay idempotent.

### CMT-011 · load-bearing annotations and directives
`hard · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Never edit or remove machine-read comments (lint and type-checker suppressions, formatter-ignore markers, tag: reason annotations scripts grep for, pragmas); report a suppression that looks like it hides a real defect instead.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `eslint-disable`, `eslint-enable`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `noqa`, `type: ignore`, `pylint: disable`, `biome-ignore`, `prettier-ignore`, `nolint`, `#pragma`, `// go:`, `# fmt: off`, `# fmt: on`, `coverage: ignore`, `istanbul ignore`
- Exceptions: The user explicitly asks for a lint-suppression cleanup as code work

### CMT-012 · dead tool directives
`soft · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Remove directives for tools the project no longer runs, but only after confirming the tool is absent from the project's configuration.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Triggers: `eslint-disable`, `eslint-enable`, `tslint:disable`, `jshint`, `jscs:`
- Exceptions: Tool presence cannot be verified: report instead of deleting

### CMT-013 · live TODO
`default · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Keep TODO and FIXME markers that point at real open work, and do not add TODOs as placeholders for work you could finish now.

- Exceptions: TODOs referring to work already done or tickets already closed: these are stale (CMT-007)

### CMT-014 · doc blocks for public API
`default · clarity · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Put genuine documentation of a public function, type or constant in the language's doc-comment form on the declaration, and leave existing doc blocks in place, tightening only verbose ones.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Private helpers: a doc block is not required; Projects whose convention is no doc blocks (criterion 6); Pre-existing loose comments outside the change's scope

### CMT-015 · comments inconsistent with local style
`default · ai-tell · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Match the surrounding file's comment density and style; a change that adds far more or differently styled comments than its neighbours reads as generated.

- Threshold: **standard:** flag comment density clearly above the file's norm · **strict:** new code carries no more comments per function than its neighbours · **relaxed:** flag only style mismatches (syntax, casing, language)
- Exceptions: The file has no comments yet and the code needs a why (CMT-001); The user asked for documentation or teaching comments

### CMT-016 · prose rules apply to comments
`default · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Apply the general prose rules (concrete wording, no puffery, no hedging, no filler) to comments and doc blocks; the comment-specific rules here override them inside comments.

- Exceptions: Prose rules that make no sense in a one-line comment (rhythm, paragraph structure)

### CMT-017 · diff-scoped comment pass
`default · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Scope a comment review to the files the caller names, otherwise to the current change against the base branch including uncommitted work, and offer a propose-only mode.


### CMT-018 · scope fence: no behaviour change
`hard · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

A comment pass changes comments only: never alter code behaviour, and never edit outside the agreed scope.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough

### CMT-019 · no additions in reduction pass
`default · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Do not add new comments during a reduction pass.

- Threshold: one occurrence is enough
- Exceptions: Moving existing documentation into a doc block (CMT-014) is a conversion, not an addition

### CMT-020 · uncertainty policy for comment deletion
`default · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

Prefer deletion for comments that fail the deletion test; a comment that only shouts (IMPORTANT, NOTE, do not remove) without a reason fails it and is removed. Keep, unchanged, a comment that states a reason or constraint that might be real, instead of guessing.

- Threshold: **standard:** delete only comments that clearly fail CMT-002; keep and report unclear ones · **strict:** delete unclear comments that this change introduced; keep unclear pre-existing ones · **relaxed:** delete only restating, banner, commented-out and history comments (CMT-003/005/006/007)

### CMT-021 · fresh-eyes review, bounded retry
`soft · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

For a large comment review, optionally use a fresh-context reviewer, audit its findings against CMT-011 and CMT-018, and retry at most once before reporting the pass as incomplete.

- Exceptions: Small diffs: review inline; a subagent costs more than it saves

### CMT-022 · comment-pass report
`soft · procedure · scope: comments · voice cannot override`

A comment pass returns only the code; add one short plain-language line only when the user must act, never a list of what was removed or rule ids.
